## New API the NEW test file locks (module exports, all pure; the module is written in the next step)
1. `clauseKey(clause)`: normalised clause path or null. Strips a leading `Chapter `, any `.` directly before `(`, surrounding spaces and a trailing `, Exception ...` part; null / '' / non-string -> null. `'Chapter 10.20.30.40.(1)(A)'` -> `'10.20.30.40(1)(A)'`; `'900.6.10(252), Exception RM 252'` -> `'900.6.10(252)'`; `'150.7.60.20(2)(B)'` unchanged.
2. `buildingOfRow(row, suiteBuildings, settings)` -> `{building, rule_id, displaced_by}`. `row.clause` via clauseKey; `suiteBuildings` is an array of building names present in the case (e.g. `['garden_suite']`). Order: (a) no clause -> `settings.buildings.no_clause_building` with rule_id `no_clause`; (b) a `buildings.displaced` entry whose `clause_prefix` the clause starts with AND whose `when_case_has` is in suiteBuildings -> that entry's `building`, rule_id its id, displaced_by its `displaced_by`; (c) the first `clause_rules` entry with a prefix the clause starts with -> its building and id; (d) else `default_building`, rule_id `default`. A row's own `building` field is ignored. Table-driven expectations (use these exact rows): `150.7.60.50(2)` garden_suite; `150.8.60.40(1)(A)` laneway_suite; `10.5.60.40(3)` other_ancillary; `10.10.60.70(1)` other_ancillary; `10.20.30.40(1)(A)` lot_wide (no suite); `10.5.50.10(3)(A)` lot_wide with no suite and garden_suite with `['garden_suite']` (rule R12, displaced_by `150.7.50.10(1)`); `10.20.30.40(1)(A)` with `['garden_suite']` lot_wide (R15); `10.20.40.10(1)(A)` main; `900.3.10(38)(A)` main; `900.6.10(252), Exception RM 252` lot_wide; `Chapter 10.20.30.40.(1)(A)` lot_wide; `200.5.1.10(2)(A)(i)` lot_wide; `10.5.100.1(2)(B)(ii)` lot_wide; no clause -> lot_wide; `999.9.9` -> unknown.
3. `measureOfRow(row, settings)`: `row.measure` when a non-empty string; else the first `buildings.measure_rules` entry with a prefix of the clauseKey; else null. Examples: `10.20.40.40(1)(A)` gfa; `10.20.40.10(1)(A)` height; `10.5.60.40(3)` storeys; `10.20.30.40(1)(A)` footprint; `10.20.40.10(2)(A)(i)` null (main-wall height is no direction measure); explicit `measure:'units'` wins.
4. `prepareRows(cases, varianceRows, settings)` -> `{rows, skipped}`. Each input row is copied with added `building`, `rule_id`, `displaced_by`, `measure` (via measureOfRow), `clause_key`; the suite buildings of a case are the `buildings.suite_roles` keys present in `case.buildings` (a case has `buildings: {main?:{class,status,applicant}, garden_suite?:..., laneway_suite?:...}`; a case without `buildings` has none). Duplicate rule (data `buildings.duplicate_rule`): two rows of one case with the same `building` (after the table), same non-null `city_limit` and same non-null `applicant_figure` are one fact: the row with `displaced_by` set is skipped and listed `{case, ordinal, reason:'duplicate_displaced'}`; the other stays; rows without both figures are never duplicates. Test the A0461 shape: row ordinal 2 clause `10.5.50.10(3)(A)` and ordinal 3 clause `150.7.50.10(1)(A)`, both city_limit 69.15, applicant_figure 60.65, case with `buildings.garden_suite` -> `rows` has one row (ordinal 3), `skipped` has ordinal 2. Same two rows in a case WITHOUT a suite stay two rows.
5. `unitsOf(caseObj, settings)` -> array of scored units `{id, case, building, class, status, applicant, parcel_id, held, new_build}`. A case without `buildings` is normalised to `{main:{class: applicant_class, status: new_build === false ? 'existing' : 'new', applicant}}` (so every existing fixture of the old test file still works). Facts: `suite_new` = any `suite_roles` building with `status === 'new'`; `main_status` = `buildings.main.status`, default `settings.buildings.main_status.default`. Pick the first `buildings.scoring` entry whose `when` matches (`suite_new` equal when present, `main_status` in the list when present); `score` tokens: `main` -> the main building when present; `suite` -> every suite_roles building present with status new, in `buildings.list` order. `id` is the case id for main, else `<case>:<building>`. `held` = building in `buildings.held`. `new_build` = status === 'new'. Tests (ruling 3, "3 y"): suite-only (main existing, garden suite new) -> exactly one unit `<case>:garden_suite`; both new -> two units (main, suite); no suite -> the main only whatever its status; a laneway suite new on an existing house -> one unit `<case>:laneway_suite` with `held: true`.
6. `adaptBuildingFile(file, settings)` -> `{cases, varianceRows}` from the INC-7 input shape (`file.cases[]`: `case_id`, `parcel_id`, `applicant.building_type.{golden_p_type, golden_ex_type, golden_p_suite_type, proposed_25_text}`, `applicant.{gfa,height,storeys,footprint,units}.{value}` (gfa may carry `suite_value`), `varied_clauses[]`: `ordinal`, `clause.value`, `permitted.value`, `requested.value`, `permitted.as_printed`, `requested.as_printed`, `city_granted.value`, `measure`, `building` (ignored)). Output case: `{case: case_id, parcel_id, applicant_class: class_map[golden_p_type] ?? null, new_build: <main status is new>, buildings: {main: {class, status, applicant:{gfa,height,storeys,footprint,units from .value}}, plus garden_suite / laneway_suite when class_map maps golden_p_suite_type: {class, status:'new', applicant:{gfa: gfa.suite_value (number) else null, others null}}}}`; main status: `new` when `proposed_25_text` matches any regex of `buildings.main_status.new_text_patterns` (case-insensitive), else `buildings.main_status.default`. The class map is a NEW setting the orchestrator adds before the next step: `buildings.class_map = {"detached_house":"detached_house","detached_houseplex":"detached_houseplex","garden":"garden_suite","laneway":"laneway_suite"}` (the red tests may read it from settings; if absent in the file at your time of writing, build the cfg with it set). Row out: `{case, ordinal, clause: clause.value, city_row: true, granted: city_granted.value, city_limit: permitted.value (number or null), applicant_figure: requested.value (number or null), text: lower-cased permitted.as_printed + ' ' + requested.as_printed, measure: measure ?? undefined}`. Test with a 3-case inline mini-file: one new detached house, one existing house plus garden suite (suite_value 99.22), one with `golden_p_suite_type:'laneway'` and a house existing.

## Behaviour tests on the scorer (same new file)
D-2 (ruling): (a) `scoreDirection` `pass` is the exact test `correct * 100 >= threshold_pct * denominator` (9 of 10 pass, 22 of 25 fail, 23 of 25 pass, 17 of 19 fail, 18 of 20 pass) and `required` stays ceil; (b) a measure is excluded for a case iff the keyed applicant figure is null: output `direction.<m>.excluded_cases` (array of unit ids) and `scoreInc7` returns `manifest: {excluded:[{case, measure, reason:'applicant_figure_null'}], denominators:{<measure>:n}, units:[ids], skipped_rows:[...], disclosures:[...], digest}` where `digest` is a 12-hex sha256 prefix of the canonical JSON of the manifest without `digest`, identical on two runs, and changing when one excluded case is added; the excluded list for the fixture `cases6` on gfa is empty and on a copy with c5 applicant `{}` is `[{case:'c5', measure:'gfa', reason:'applicant_figure_null'}, ...one entry per measure]`; (c) our not-evaluated counts as wrong stays: a unit whose class is null is `not_evaluated` and in the denominator.
D-3: closeness `quantile_method: 'floor_index'` (oracle-compare.mjs:24 quant: index `floor(q*(n-1))` on the sorted values): ratios 0.77, 0.87, 0.92, 1.0 (n=4) give `median 0.895`, `spread {kind:'iqr', q1: 0.77, q3: 0.92, iqr: 0.15}`; n=5 (0.7..1.1) still q1 0.8, q3 1.0; setting `quantile_method:'linear'` gives the type-7 values (n=4: q1 0.845, q3 0.94 after 3 dp rounding of 0.8450 and 0.9400, iqr 0.095); unknown method -> `validateSettings` has `quantile_method_unknown:<x>`. Closeness uses units with `new_build` (status new) so a suite-only case contributes its suite, not its existing house.
D-4: (a) off-scope rows as data: a City row with clause `230.5.1.10(6)` and `our_verdict:'EXCEEDS'` classes MISSED with `cause` from the setting (`catch.off_scope`), and so does a row whose `text` contains `bicycle` with no clause; with the setting `off_scope: []` the same row is CAUGHT (limit_match true): proves it is data, not code; (b) relative limits: clause `150.7.60.50(2)` with `our_verdict:'EXCEEDS'`, city_limit null -> CAUGHT with no limit comparison; with `relative_rules: []` it is NOT SCORED (limit_match null); (c) second CAUGHT-ESTIMATE trigger: City row, `our_verdict:'MAY EXCEED'`, city_limit 100 vs our_limit 150 (limit_match false) -> CAUGHT-ESTIMATE; (d) `classifyRow` accepts facts `{city_row, our_verdict, limit_match, relative, off_scope}`; (e) SC-19 wrong limits 0 with complete inputs: a WRONG LIMIT row whose unit has class and gfa/height/storeys figures (`catch.complete_inputs`) fails `wrong_limit_complete_inputs_max`; the same WRONG LIMIT row where the applicant height is null (incomplete) passes that line but still counts in `wrong_limit_max`; changing `catch.complete_inputs.measures` to `['gfa']` makes the second case complete (data); (f) `wrong_limit_named_cause_max`: a WRONG LIMIT row with a `cause` string passes, without a `cause` fails; (g) catch rows carry `clause`, `ordinal`, `building`, `off_scope`, `relative`, `cause`, `complete_inputs`.
Ruling 1 (building) in scoring: (a) a variance row counts as a variance for a unit only when its building is in `buildings.variance_buildings[unit.building]` (garden-suite height row granted does NOT flip the main unit's height; a `lot_wide` footprint row does count for main); (b) a catch row on a `garden_suite` building derives its max from the case's `buildings.garden_suite.class` (Layer 3 rows with `building_type: 'garden_suite'`), a row on `other_ancillary` has no class so derives NOT EVALUATED -> MISSED; (c) the row skipped as duplicate is absent from `catch.rows` and present in `manifest.skipped_rows`.
Ruling 3 (by building) end-to-end: `scoreDirection` on a suite-only case scores the suite against the garden_suite max (applicant suite gfa 99.22 vs max 100 -> correct) and does not score the existing main house; both-new case scores both with each its own max; no-suite case scores the main house; denominators count units.
Laneway held: a laneway-suite unit is `not_evaluated` with `held` true, is in the denominator (counts wrong), and appears in `manifest.disclosures` as `{unit:'<case>:laneway_suite', building:'laneway_suite', measure, reason:'held:laneway_suite'}` once per measure with an applicant figure; setting `buildings.held: []` makes the same unit evaluate against its max (if the Layer 3 rows exist).
